A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 49 readable pages, including Appendices A–J. Full text comparison and rendered-page checks support a reliable comparison of the text, figures, and mathematics.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C, including synthetic regression, neuron activation statistics, and MNIST-versus-Gaussian training results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix C, including generalization trends, training curves, and depth-dependent prediction errors.

M1.justification: The two-layer ReLU model, squared-error objective, gradient-descent procedure, and BEoS framework are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Beta-radial distributions, spherical data, mixtures of lines, and MNIST-versus-Gaussian regression settings. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain the same GD-trained models across input geometries and the same noise-reference baselines. No competing method is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Experimental settings and metrics in Section 4 and Appendix C are identical. For example, Section 4.1 retains width 1000, learning rate 0.4, 20000 epochs, and clean-MSE slope estimation.

E4.justification: The neuron activation analysis, Hessian-norm tracking, memorization curves, and MNIST depth-versus-error analysis are retained unchanged in Figures 4–9.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 reports averaging over six random seeds in both versions. The statistical reporting and uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: All plotted outcomes and reported numerical results are unchanged. Section 4.2 retains final true MSE values of 1.0249 for spherical inputs and 0.07 for the mixture of lines.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, theorems, and proofs, including Appendices D–J, are unchanged. The removed introductory summary of classical generalization-bound techniques is explanatory prose, not a change to mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and discussion retain the same claims about data shatterability, radial concentration, spherical interpolation, and adaptation to intrinsic dimension.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and limitations are unchanged, including the concentration index's restricted applicability and the theoretical restriction to two-layer ReLU networks.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical implementation and data-generation details, hyperparameters, normalization, and monitoring procedures. No technical resource or code/data access information changes.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and substantive research positioning are unchanged. Shortening the introductory description of classical bounds does not alter the stated relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 corrects Alexander Clonginer to Alexander Cloninger, revises author/contact text, removes the conference header, shortens the Technical novelty paragraph, and fixes punctuation spacing in Section 4.2. The section organization and remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 rearranges the author block into four columns, introduces a correspondence footnote, and removes the repeated conference-header text, with limited text reflow. Figures 1–9 and their captions, axes, legends, and placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides small editorial corrections and formatting changes while retaining identical scientific arguments, proofs, experiments, results, reproducibility details, and limitations. The author-name correction and shortened introductory explanation do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
